text:
Maya: Heads-up — starting canary for mantis13b-int4 (quant v2) on dedicated pools. seeing 2/50 nodes hit OOM during generation stage when requests hit KV priming. logs show sharp memory climb at 'kv_alloc' just before 'decoder_step'.
Alex: ugh. what were the batch / max_new_tokens settings for the canary?
Maya: default batch_size=4, batch_window_ms=12, max_new_tokens=256. reduced to 64 locally and it completed without OOM but higher latency.
Carl: could be fragmentation from int4 allocator + large max_new. try soft-evict + bump kv_trim_threshold. also consider lowering slot_reserve for canary.
Maya: noted. quick test: lowered max_new_tokens to 80 + soft_evict=true and ran 100 requests — no OOMs but tiny quality diffs on long-form prompts.
Jen: can we run the eval harness across the canary and baseline to quantify quality delta? run top-100 promptset and compare rouge/bertscore. if degradation < 0.5% we can accept.
Maya: starting eval now. patch I'm testing:
```
model: mantis13b-int4-v2
serve_config:
  max_new_tokens: 80
  batch_window_ms: 12
  batch_size: 4
  soft_evict: true
  kv_trim_threshold: 0.65
  slot_reserve: 0.06
```
Alex: also suggest enabling prefix_kv_cache=true for these workloads; avoids hot allocation for repeated prefixes. but watch memory SLO.
Carl: if frag is the cause, also run a short mem-defrag after N requests: `curl /admin/defrag?n=50` (dev-only). helps on metal.
Maya: infra-bot triggered canary deploy: deploy #mantis13b-int4-v2 to pool-dedicated-3
infra-bot: deploy started — canary on 5 hosts. monitoring memory + oom counts.
Maya: eval finished — quality delta: BERTScore -0.3%, ROUGE-L -0.4% on long-form, negligible on chatty prompts. latency +120ms median.
Jen: sounds within acceptable tradeoff if cost benefits are good. what's the unit-cost delta?
Maya: int4 reduces token cost ~2.6x vs fp16 on this model; but enabling soft_evict increases CPU overhead maybe +5% infra. overall still ~2.4x cheaper.
Alex: rollout plan: 1) widen canary to 20 hosts with the patched config, 2) run smoke eval every hour, 3) if OOMs stay <=1% and quality delta <0.5% after 8h, promote to prod with gradual rollout + soft rollback.
Carl: add autoretry policy to route larger max_new_tokens to fallback fp16 variant when mem pressure > 75% to avoid hard OOMs.
Maya: created rollout doc and PR for route policy + default config. job: https://git.internal/r/redwood/mantis/onboard/PR-412
Jen: please add an eval-run step to CI that compares quantized v2 vs baseline fp16 nightly. we saw small drift — want to catch regressions.
Maya: good call. I'll add `eval-run --suite=mantis-longform --compare=fp16` to the job.
Alex: one more thing — some users saw truncated outputs because clients rely on default max_new_tokens. consider lowering global default for mantis family to 128 and note in release notes.
Maya: will update defaults in model catalog + add a note under 'known limits' for long-form generation.
infra-bot: canary widened to 20 hosts (completed). no new OOMs since config change.
Carl: leave monitoring on for 24h and then proceed with staged rollout. also capture allocator histograms for forensic if OOM reappears.
Maya: tagging ops for 24h watch and will notify product once metrics stable. thanks team :thumbsup:
